summary: This bill requires the Attorney General and dozens of federal agencies to report to Congress on every federal criminal statutory and regulatory offense—including each offense's elements, penalties, 15-year prosecution or referral history, and mens rea requirement—and to publish public online indexes of all such offenses.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates reports and public indexes on federal criminal offenses but explicitly states in subsection (e) that nothing shall be construed to require or authorize appropriations. While the underlying goal of identifying crimes to cut could indirectly reduce enforcement costs, the legislation itself creates no new spending and has no direct fiscal impact.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill makes no changes to healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
The bill does not address firearms regulations or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions in the bill relate to immigration enforcement, pathways, or border policy.
The legislation has no bearing on reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not affect military or defense spending or policy.
While the EPA is among the agencies required to report on its criminal regulatory offenses, the bill itself only requires cataloging existing offenses and does not alter environmental regulations.
No provisions address welfare programs, food assistance, or related entitlements.
The bill does not engage with education policy or funding.
The bill requires reporting on all federal criminal offenses, including drug-related ones, but does not change any drug laws or enforcement policies.

The core purpose of the bill is to compile comprehensive lists of federal criminal statutory and regulatory offenses (including penalties, prosecution data, and mens rea requirements) to facilitate identifying and cutting unnecessary crimes. This directly advances criminal justice reform by highlighting overcriminalization, particularly regulatory offenses.
No provisions relate to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill explicitly prohibits new appropriations and has no impact on deficit spending or debt reduction.
The legislation does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions concern foreign aid or international assistance.
The bill has no connection to voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance policy.
No provisions relate to worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.
